cards.design_implication: If an optical-only calibration of (g-i) colour to M*/Li is adopted, the design must explicitly account for the stated precision limit (≲0.1 dex 1σ) and propagate uncertainties arising from stellar evolution model dependencies.
does_not_establish: The exact functional form or coefficients of the (g-i)–M*/Li relation.
Whether this calibration accuracy holds for populations outside the GAMA sample.
The underlying causes of the uncertainties in stellar evolution models.
cards.evidence_excerpt: Further, we use the observed relation between restframe (g−i) and M*/Li for real GAMA galaxies to argue that, modulo uncertainties in the stellar evolution models themselves, (g−i) colour can in practice be used to estimate M*/Li to an accuracy of ≲0.1 dex (1σ).
limitations: The claimed accuracy applies specifically to real GAMA galaxies using restframe (g-i) colour.
The precision is conditioned on remaining uncertainties in stellar evolution models.
cards.statement: The observed relation between restframe (g-i) colour and stellar mass-to-light ratio (M*/Li) allows M*/Li to be estimated with an accuracy of ≲0.1 dex (1σ) for GAMA galaxies, modulo uncertainties in stellar evolution models.

cards.design_implication: When designing spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting for this dataset, the inclusion of NIR photometry may degrade fit quality and should be tested against optical-only fits to verify whether improved constraints outweigh the reduction in fit consistency.
does_not_establish: The specific statistical metrics used to determine the drop in fit quality.
The specific causes of the degradation (e.g., library issues vs. data issues), although these are mentioned as possibilities elsewhere.
Whether NIR data are universally unsuitable for other similar surveys.
cards.evidence_excerpt: Although the GAMA database does include near-infrared (NIR) photometry, we show that the quality of our stellar population synthesis fits is significantly poorer when these NIR data are included.
limitations: The statement applies specifically to the stellar population synthesis fits described in this catalogue.
The abstract does not quantify the degree of 'significantly poorer' beyond the qualitative description.
cards.statement: The quality of stellar population synthesis fits significantly decreases when near-infrared (NIR) photometry is included alongside optical data for GAMA galaxies.
